Let exactness be with respect to the measure \(d\mu_\tau\). Write

\[
m_{2k}=\int_{-1}^1 x^{2k}\,d\mu_\tau(x)=\frac{2}{2k+1}+2\tau .
\]

For the three-point Gaussian rule with nodes \(-a_\tau,0,a_\tau\), let \(s=a_\tau^2\). Exactness at degrees \(2,4\) gives

\[
s=\frac{m_4}{m_2}
=\frac{\frac25+2\tau}{\frac23+2\tau}
=\frac{3(1+5\tau)}{5(1+3\tau)}.
\]

Thus \(3/5<s<1\) for \(\tau>0\), and

\[
\tau=\frac{3-5s}{15s-15}.
\]

Now set \(t=b^2\). The seven-node nodal polynomial is

\[
L(x)=x(x^2-1)(x^2-s)(x^2-t).
\]

A seven-node interpolatory rule is exact through degree \(11\) iff

\[
\int L(x)q(x)\,d\mu_\tau(x)=0
\]

for every \(\deg q\le 4\). By evenness, only \(q=x,x^3\) matter. Also \(L(\pm1)=0\), so the atoms at \(\pm1\) do not contribute. Hence the two conditions use only Lebesgue moments:

\[
\int_{-1}^1 x^2(x^2-1)(x^2-s)(x^2-t)\,dx=0,
\]

\[
\int_{-1}^1 x^4(x^2-1)(x^2-s)(x^2-t)\,dx=0.
\]

Using \(\int_{-1}^1 x^{2k}\,dx=2/(2k+1)\), these become

\[
(9s-5)+(9-21s)t=0,
\]

\[
(-35+55s)+(55-99s)t=0.
\]

Eliminating \(t\),

\[
(5-9s)(55-99s)=(35-55s)(9-21s),
\]

so

\[
33s^2-30s+5=0.
\]

Thus

\[
s=\frac{15\pm2\sqrt{15}}{33}.
\]

Only

\[
s=\frac{15+2\sqrt{15}}{33}
\]

lies in \((3/5,1)\). Therefore

\[
a_\tau=\sqrt{\frac{15+2\sqrt{15}}{33}},
\qquad
b=\sqrt{\frac{15-2\sqrt{15}}{33}}.
\]

Substituting \(s\) into the formula for \(\tau\),

\[
\tau=\frac{3-5s}{15s-15}
=\frac{\sqrt{15}-1}{30}.
\]

The weights are then uniquely determined by interpolation. For the ordinary integral they are

\[
A_0=\frac1{21},\qquad
B=\frac{62}{175}+\frac{\sqrt{15}}{50},\qquad
C=\frac{62}{175}-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{50},\qquad
D=\frac{256}{525}.
\]

Since \(d\mu_\tau=dx+\tau(\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)\), the endpoint weight becomes

\[
A=A_0+\tau
=\frac{7\sqrt{15}+3}{210}.
\]

All four weights are positive. The equations above force \(s\), then \(t\), then the interpolatory weights, so the nested rule is unique.

\[
\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{15}-1}{30}}
\]
